title: Naming parts of my body
keyIdea: Your body has parts with names. Your head is at the top, your tummy is in the middle, and your toes are at the bottom on your feet. Arms bend at the elbow and legs bend at the knee. Each part helps you do things: legs help you walk, hands help you clap, your mouth helps you eat and arms give a hug.

kid: This is your head. It is at the top. Your tummy is in the middle. Your toes are at the bottom, on your feet. Can you touch them?
Sing it! Head, shoulders, knees and toes. The song goes from the top down. Touch each part as you sing.
Your arm can bend. It bends at the elbow. Your leg can bend too. It bends at the knee. Bend, then make it straight!
Each part helps you. Legs help you walk and jump. Hands help you clap. Your mouth helps you eat. Arms give a big hug.
adult: At two and three, children learn to name and point to the main parts of the body: head, shoulders, tummy, arms, elbows, hands, legs, knees, feet and toes. They also start to say simple things each part does, such as legs for walking. This is early science vocabulary, and it also helps a child tell you where something hurts.

Toddlers learn body words best through touch and movement. Naming a part while they touch it, and songs such as Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes, link the word to the place. Working from the top of the body to the bottom gives them a map: head at the top, tummy in the middle, feet at the bottom. Bending an elbow and a knee shows that these are the joints where arms and legs fold.

Common mistakes to watch for: mixing up elbow and knee, since both are bends; calling the whole leg a foot or the whole arm a hand; saying toes for fingers; and pointing to the chest for tummy. Correct by touching both parts and naming them side by side, for example: this is your elbow on your arm, this is your knee on your leg.

In the lab your child taps head, tummy, hands and toes on Kit, taps the song parts in order from top to bottom, drags a hand and a foot to bend the elbow and the knee, taps the part that helps Kit walk, clap, eat and hug, and builds Kit by putting the head on top, the arms at the sides and the legs at the bottom.

familyTip: At bath time or while dressing, play Touch Your: say "Touch your elbow!" and then swap so your child gives the orders. Sing Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes slowly, then faster. Ask, "What do your legs help you do?" and let your child show you.

visual.caption: Top half or bottom half of the body? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: find body parts on Kit, tap the song in order, bend an elbow and a knee, find the part for each job, and build Kit.

practice.hint: Touch the very top of you. What part is up there?
practice.explain: Your head is at the top of your body. Your tummy is in the middle and your feet are at the bottom.

practice.prompt: Kit takes {n} big steps across the room. Which body part helps Kit walk?
practice.hint: Which parts move when you walk across the room?
practice.explain: Legs help Kit walk. Each of the {n} steps is one leg moving forward, then the other.

practice.prompt: Your leg bends in the middle. What is that part called?
practice.hint: Your arm bends at the elbow. The leg has its own bend.
practice.explain: Your leg bends at the knee. Your arm bends at the elbow, so they are different bends.

practice.prompt: Mia claps her hands {n} times. What does she clap with?
practice.hint: Clap is a noise you make by bringing two parts together. Which two?
practice.explain: Mia claps {n} times with her hands. Feet can stamp, but hands clap.

pool.hint: Look all the way down. What is at the end of your legs?
pool.explain: Toes are on your feet, at the very bottom. The parts on your hands are fingers.

pool.hint: The song goes down the body. What is at the very bottom?
pool.explain: Head, shoulders, knees and toes. The song goes from the top of you to the bottom.

pool.prompt: Your arm bends in the middle. What is that called?
pool.hint: Bend your arm and touch the pointy bit in the middle.
pool.explain: Your arm bends at the elbow. The knee is the bend in your leg.

pool.prompt: What helps you eat your apple?
pool.hint: Where does the apple go when you take a bite?
pool.explain: Your mouth helps you eat. You bite and chew with it.

pool.prompt: Gran opens her arms. She gives you {n} big hugs. What does she hug with?
pool.hint: Which parts wrap around you in a hug?
pool.explain: Gran hugs with her arms. They wrap around you all {n} times.

pool.hint: It is between your head and your legs. Pat it!
pool.explain: Your tummy is in the middle of your body, between your head and your legs.

pool.prompt: Leo jumps {n} times on the spot. What helps him jump?
pool.hint: What pushes you up off the floor?
pool.explain: Legs and feet push Leo up off the floor for all {n} jumps. His knees bend to help.
